Anisotropy Dependence on direction, such as different widths in a four-plane and its six-dimensional complement. A favorable diagnostic shape still needs supporting stress. 11.4
Ansatz A proposed form of an equation or field to test. Substitution can establish consequences or closure; choosing the form is an additional premise. 4.2; 11.4; 12.2
Antiunitary map A norm-preserving transformation involving complex conjugation. The reviewed opposite-charge construction also reflects a coordinate and reverses the time history. 11.1
Anticommutator {A,B}=AB+BA\{A,B\}=AB+BA{A,B}=AB+BA. Its vanishing or specified value controls Clifford products and the angular repair. 2.2; 6.1; 10.1
Antiparticle; antipattern An opposite-label solution is a candidate comparison. Identification with observed antiparticles, including their physical interaction behavior, remains open. 11.1; 14
Available versus occupied states A count of mathematical labels does not establish that all are physical portions of a sustained pattern. That bridge is part of the count-selection problem. 3.1; 3.3
Beta integral A radial integration identity expressible as a ratio of gamma functions. It evaluates the bubble norm. It is unrelated to the matrix β\betaβ. 6.3
Bilinear An expression linear in each of two factors, including spinor products and spinor-to-vector maps. Its transformation law can differ from each factor's. 6.4; 9.2
Binomial coefficient (ab)=a!/[b!(a−b)!]\binom ab=a!/[b!(a-b)!](ba​)=a!/[b!(a−b)!], counting selections or the equivalent exponent configurations used here. 3.1
Biradial profile A profile depending on two physical radii, with rotational symmetry inside each specified group of directions. 11.4; different 2+8 reduction, 12.2
Blade A wedge or corresponding Clifford product of independent directions. Its degree counts those directions. 8.1; 8.4
Bound/free directions Directions involved in a pattern's bound structure versus its remaining extension. A proposed 4+6 reference split is not automatically a particle's bound/free split. 2.1; 6.3; 9.3
Bracket certificate Exact inequalities locating a target between neighboring predictions, excluding all other indices using monotonicity. 5.2
Bridge A derived connection between two descriptions, including their equations, carriers and conserved quantities. Similar labels alone do not supply it. 13.3
Bubble The explicit decaying spatial spinor profile in section 6. Its name does not imply a material wall or an additional physical space. 6.1
Calibration Fixing an input using observations. Distinct from deriving it from dynamics, and from testing other outputs after that input is fixed. 1.1; 4
Canonical momentum Derivative of the Lagrangian with respect to a field's time derivative. Derivative interactions change it and therefore change phase charges. 12.1
Carrier; module; fibre A carrier/module is the component system acted on by the equations or representation. Fibre denotes components at a point. These words introduce no additional physical manifold. 7.1; 7.3
Casimir operator A combination of generators invariant under the relevant group. It labels rotation types or channels, rather than supplying a physical interaction by itself. spin, 6.2; color, 8.2; endomorphisms, 8.4
Central phase; central U(1)U(1)U(1) A common phase rotation commuting with every matrix in the specified group. Its weights need a physical source interpretation before being called electric charges. 9.1
Centroid A density-weighted spatial center. Recentring an angular operator on it does not repair the explicit reciprocal-interaction counterexample. 10.2
Character; determinant character A one-dimensional representation. The determinant records the total phase accumulated by three component labels. 9.1
Charge weight versus integrated charge A weight is a transformation eigenvalue per component. A physical integrated source also depends on its current, norm and normalization. 9.1; 10.2; 12.1
Chirality A sign branch defined by an oriented Clifford or Hodge operation in the stated construction. Its relation to observed interaction handedness requires a separate bridge. 7.1; 8.1; 9.4
Clifford algebra Matrix multiplication rules encoding the spatial metric, here {γi,γj}=2δijI\{\gamma_i,\gamma_j\}=2\delta_{ij}I{γi​,γj​}=2δij​I. They organize spinor rotations and derivatives. 6.1; explicit recipe, B.1
Clock An invariant first-order rotation of component pairs under a specified action. The clock selector does not set its frequency or select the count nnn. 7.1
Closed sector A field ansatz preserved by the full stated equations: substituting it generates no omitted component structures. This alone is not an existence or stability theorem. 11.4; 12.2
Color The proposed independent SU(3) component transformation. It is not visual color, spatial topology, or a derivation of gluons or confinement. 7.4; 8.2
Commutant All linear operations commuting with the specified representation. Its size depends on the full carrier and its repeated copies. 7.1; 7.3
Commutator [A,B]=AB−BA[A,B]=AB-BA[A,B]=AB−BA, testing whether two operations can be performed in either order with the same result. 2.2; free charge, 10.1
Complex encoding Paired real components or paired ordinary real directions represented with complex notation. It supplies no second physical space. 2.1
Complete band/channel Every component or label belonging to the stated band or eigenspace is retained. Selectively keeping a smaller set changes the theorem's premises. 7.2; 8.1
Conditional result A consequence established under specified additional physical or mathematical assumptions, without declaring those assumptions experimentally established. 1.1
Conjugate-fundamental triplet The three-component representation transformed by the complex-conjugate matrices of the fundamental. Its invariant products differ from those of a same-type triplet. 8.2; 9.1
Connection A rule for comparing component phases or orientations at neighboring positions. The depth-five texture connection is stipulated, not derived as a common particle solution. 9.4
Contact term An action term depending on field values at the same point. Its existence and symmetries must be checked separately from a full force law. 8.3
Covariance Transformation of an equation or field construction in the prescribed way when coordinates and components are transformed together. 6.2; 12.5
Critical nonlinearity The particular density power in the stationary bubble equation. It is an equation-specific assumption, not a demonstrated common law across all depths. 6.1
Current A field expression carrying a spatial or spacetime index. A conserved Noether current must satisfy the appropriate continuity equation on solutions; a source called “current” need not already do so. 8.3; 12.1
Decomposable form A form expressible as one wedge of independent vectors. For the pure-pencil proof the two-form satisfies v2∧v2=0v_2\wedge v_2=0v2​∧v2​=0. 9.3
Depth Number of ordinary physical spatial directions involved in the proposed pattern classification. It is not the number of component labels. 2.1; 2.2
Derivative jet Field values and some of their derivatives at the same point. They can supply distinct determinant slots only when their actual independence is shown. 8.3; 12.1
Determinant An alternating volume expression; zero for dependent columns. For complex-encoded components it also records phase. 2.2; 9.1; 11.5; 12.1
Dilation Rescaling physical spatial widths, with amplitude rescaled when norms or phase actions must remain fixed. Its first variation yields a necessary stress balance. 11.4; 12.5
Dirac operator The first-order Clifford contraction of spatial derivatives. Factors of iii, mass terms and dimension are specified locally. 6.1; 10.1
Dispersal threshold Energy of the specified spread-out comparison at fixed conserved quantities. Binding below it does not exclude every other decay or deformation. 12.2
Doublet; triplet; singlet Representations with two, three or one component label under the indicated group. A singlet is invariant. Different doublets need not be the same physical spin system. 7.4; 9.1
Eigenvalue; eigenspace A multiplier under an operator, and the set of vectors with that multiplier. Its multiplicity is the eigenspace's dimension. 2.2
Endomorphism A linear map from a component space to itself. Section 8.4 studies its transformation under rotations. 8.4
Equivariance; intertwiner A map respects the group action: transforming the input and then applying the map agrees with transforming its output. 6.2; 9.2
Exterior algebra; form Antisymmetric combinations describing oriented elements. Degree counts the number of directions combined, not mass level or occupied portions. 8.1; 9.1
Field and field component Values assigned on physical spacetime and the numbers needed to describe them locally. Components are not separate physical positions. 2.1
Finite norm Convergence of the integrated squared field magnitude. It is weaker than a complete finite-energy, sustained particle construction. 6.3; 12.2
Flag A nested list of spatial subspaces. A selected base and complement do not automatically select the complete list. 9.3
Flux; winding Integrated circulation of the stipulated connection and its integer texture winding. Their physical realization remains an input to the depth-five example. 9.4
Foldy–Wouthuysen map A free momentum-dependent change of component basis separating energy branches. It dresses an operator nonlocally in position; it does not redefine literal position. 10.2
Fourier expansion/transform A mathematical decomposition into frequency or momentum components. Its terms are not automatically separately resonating physical objects. 3.3; 11.3
Free equation The specified kinetic/restoring equation before additional interactions. Conservation for it must be retested after coupling. 10.1; 10.2
Frequency, ordinary/angular/fundamental/registered Cycles per second; radians per second; the portions' common cycle rate; and the proposed count-multiplied measured rate. These must not be interchanged. 2.3; 3.2; 3.3
Gamma function Integral function extending factorials; appears in the norm formula. Distinct from Clifford matrices and chirality operators. 6.3
Gap A positive lower bound for the specified response operator after frequency and nonlinear corrections. Its positivity supports the stated relaxation bound. 12.3; 12.4
Generator; Lie algebra An infinitesimal transformation and the commutator algebra of such generators. Lowercase su(3)\mathfrak{su}(3)su(3) refers to the algebra of the group SU(3)SU(3)SU(3). 6.2; 8.2
Geometric mean ab\sqrt{ab}ab​ for positive a,ba,ba,b, the midpoint in logarithmic distance. Numerical proximity does not derive a mixed physical branch. 4.3; 5.2
Global/local symmetry A transformation with the same parameter everywhere, or with a parameter varying over spacetime. Global invariance does not alone establish the local version. 12.1
Graded commutativity Exchanging exterior forms of degrees p,qp,qp,q multiplies their wedge by (−1)pq(-1)^{pq}(−1)pq. Odd-degree self-wedges therefore vanish. 8.3
Gram matrix Matrix of inner products among a set of vectors or matrices, here used to check clock/color commutator norms. B.3
Green function Response to a point source for a specified linear operator; used to reconstruct the response to a distributed source. It is not a mediator particle. 12.4
Hamiltonian Energy function in the real clock example, or time-evolution operator in the first-order field equation. The meaning is specified locally. 7.1; 10.1
Handedness; helicity A specified kinetic branch or rotation weight about the observer's spatial direction. Neither is automatically identical to every use of chirality. 6.4; 9.4
Hermitian Equal to complex conjugate transpose. The finite generators and Clifford matrices use stated Hermitian conventions. 6.1
Hessian Second variation of the constrained energy. Positivity in tested directions establishes only that tested scope. 12.2
Hodge star Metric- and orientation-dependent map from an oriented form to its complementary form in the same physical directions. 8.1; B.3
IDOS Integrated density of states: cumulative number of available labels below a cutoff. It is not automatically an occupied count. 3.1
Inertia, complete Response of the complete localized solution's energy and momentum under motion, including its supporting stress. 12.5
Inner product; norm Component overlap and magnitude, locally or integrated over space. Their mathematical use introduces no Born probability law. 2.2; 6.3
Integrated color neutrality Vanishing of all integrated traceless color charges. It need not hold pointwise in the density. 12.2
Invariant Unchanged under the transformations specified in the claim. The transformation group and whether parameters are global must be named. 7.1; 8.2; 12.1
Irreducible/minimal representation A representation with no smaller invariant decomposition / the specified smallest spinor carrier. Multiplicity or a larger carrier can change the conclusions. 7.1; 7.3
Isometry A map preserving the stated inner product or squared norm. The odd-shadow map needs its 1/21/\sqrt21/2​ normalization. 8.1
Isotropic annihilator Complex-encoded directions with zero bilinear quadratic form whose Clifford action annihilates a spinor. It does not make real Euclidean directions null. 9.2; 9.3
Kernel; rank Inputs mapped to zero / number of independent outputs. A rank theorem depends on which complete map and carrier were specified. 2.2; 7.2; 8.1
Kinetic term/order Derivative part of the action or equation. First- and second-order candidate dynamics have different canonical structures. 7.1; 10.1; 12.1
Laue condition Vanishing integrated spatial stress under the stated localization, conservation and stationary-rest-stress hypotheses. 12.5
Linear response The first-order response around a specified configuration. It does not establish arbitrary-amplitude stability. 12.4
Localization; support Concentration near a spatial region / the region where a field is nonzero. Decaying tails may have infinite support but finite norm or energy. 6.3; 12.2
Lorentz boost/scalar A transformation between uniformly moving spacetime frames / a component with the stated scalar transformation law. The latter is an extra premise of section 12. 12.1; 12.5
Magnetic moment; ggg diagnostic A moment of current / its specified dimensionless ratio to charge and spin using the comparison coupling. It is not yet an IDWT electron prediction. 11.3
Mass state versus flavor A state labeled by a mass eigenvalue versus an interaction label. The neutrino count test uses mass states. 4.2
Middle form Degree mmm in 2m2m2m directions, so its Hodge complement has the same degree. 8.1
Monomial; degree A product of coordinate powers / their summed exponent. These label the cumulative count. 3.1
Multiplicity Number of repeated representation copies or eigenvectors sharing an eigenvalue. Repeated real-type copies can restore a clock. 2.2; 7.2; 7.3
Noether charge Integrated current associated with a continuous action symmetry, conserved on solutions if boundary flux vanishes. 12.1
Normal direction An ordinary spatial direction perpendicular to a specified subspace. “Normal six” is not automatically the electron's bound six. 8.2; 9.3
Normalization Specifying a component norm, kinetic coefficient or physical source scale. These are different operations and must not be conflated. 4.1; 9.1; 12.1
Operator A rule acting on components or fields. Differential operators also act on their spatial dependence. 2.2; 10.1
Orbital contribution Coordinate-dependent part of a spatial field rotation generator. Here it is not the electron's external orbit around a nucleus. 9.4; 11.2
Parity Even/odd exterior degree, or a specified spatial reflection symmetry according to context. These uses are distinguished in their calculations. 8.2; 8.3; 11.1
Pauli matrices Three Hermitian two-by-two matrices used for spin and tensor-product recipes. Repeated copies act on distinct algebraic factors. 6.4; 9.4; B.1
Phase; phase locking Position in an oscillation cycle / fixed relative phases at a common frequency. Locking need not make all portions reach a crest simultaneously. 3.3
Phase action A canonical quantity associated with a component phase. In the interacting action only the stated symmetry combinations are conserved; the individual contributions need not be. These quantities need not be integers. 12.1; 12.2
Polarization Relative directions, magnitudes and phases of an oscillatory field's components. Linear, circular and elliptical cases are explained explicitly. 6.4
Positive-energy projection Retention of the positive free-energy branch. It changes the norm measure and need not require a positive-β\betaβ seed. 11.3
Positive completion Squared norm of a component mismatch that supplies both coupling and its square terms. Positivity alone is not full stability. 11.5; 12.1
Projector An operation satisfying P2=PP^2=PP2=P, selecting a component subspace. Dynamical closure under the full equation needs a separate check. 2.2; 8.2; 9.3
Projected norm measure Fourier weight including the positive-energy factor (1+sM/Ep)/2(1+sM/E_p)/2(1+sM/Ep​)/2, normalized by NsN_sNs​. Corrected explicitly in this draft. 11.3
Pullback; contraction Restricting a form to a subspace / inserting a vector to remove one form index. A four-form must be contracted before the stated three-dimensional restriction. 8.3
Pure spinor/pencil A spinor with maximal isotropic annihilator / a two-dimensional family all of whose nonzero members are pure. 9.2; 9.3
Quartic/sextic potential Terms of degree four/six in field amplitudes, such as ρ2,ρ3\rho^2,\rho^3ρ2,ρ3. Their signs control the stated focusing and defocusing contributions. 12.1
Quaternionic type A real representation with quaternion algebra in its commutant, providing three imaginary skew directions. 7.1
Quiet sector The exact second-order ansatz with zero singlets and retained triplet texture. “Quiet” does not mean that the triplet phases stop evolving. 12.2
Reciprocal interaction Both patterns respond through the same action, including field backreaction, rather than one being a prescribed receiver. 10.2; 12.1
Relative equilibrium A configuration stationary in shape while component phases advance at their specified rates. The numerical quiet core has two such rates. 12.2
Representation A rule assigning matrices or operators to transformations while preserving how those transformations compose. 6.1; 7.4
Residual; convergence Equation mismatch for a computed profile / evidence that refinement approaches the continuum problem. A discrete small residual is not a continuum existence proof. 12.2
Routh functional Energy minus phase frequencies times conserved actions, used for the fixed-frequency stationary and relaxation tests. 12.3
Sector A classification of pattern depth or a preserved solution ansatz, as stated locally. It is not an additional physical manifold. 3.2; 12.2
Seed Constant component data from which an explicit spatial profile is constructed. Its spin and β\betaβ signs do not by themselves fix complete physical observables. 6.1; 11.2
Shadow The specified odd-dimensional form channel induced from its containing even-dimensional spatial construction. It is an additional premise. 8.1
Simplex Higher-dimensional generalization of a segment, triangle or tetrahedron. The count uses a simplex in exponent labels without proving the particle's physical shape. 3.1
Skew; nondegenerate A real matrix with JT=−JJ^T=-JJT=−J / an invertible pairing with no unpaired nonzero direction. 7.1
Source law The physical rule relating field data and conserved current to reciprocal response. A charge-weight table alone does not supply it. 8.3; 10.2
Spatial band All chosen spatial polynomial labels through a degree cutoff, combined with component data and a decaying envelope. 7.2
Spin; spinor; Spin(d) Rotation behavior / components carrying a spin representation / the double cover of spatial rotations retaining the spinor sign. 6.1; 6.2
Stabilizer Transformations leaving specified data fixed. Preserving a spatial flag can reduce the available normal group. 9.3
Stability Persistence against specified perturbations. Restricted Hessian positivity, binding, nonlinear stability and observed lifetime are different claims. 12.2; 12.3
Stationarity Vanishing first variation under allowed changes, or a time-independent shape under specified phase motion. It is not synonymous with full stability. 6.1; 11.4; 12.2
Stress Directional momentum flow and internal forces. Complete balance is required for the conditional localized inertia result. 11.4; 12.5
SU(2), SU(3), U(3), SO(d) Groups of determinant-one unitary two-/three-component operations, general unitary three-component operations, and real orientation-preserving spatial rotations, respectively. They specify operations, not the topology of spacetime. 6.1; 7.4; 8.2
Symmetry versus topology Symmetry concerns transformations preserving specified data or laws. Topology concerns global connectedness and holes. A group label does not establish a spatial topology. 7.4
Tensor product/direct sum Simultaneous pairs of component labels / alternative component blocks. Neither automatically supplies new physical degrees of freedom. 2.2; 9.1
Transverse/longitudinal Perpendicular/parallel to a stated direction or momentum. The reference direction must be specified. 6.4; 12.4
Virial identity Necessary balance obtained by a scale variation of a stationary constrained functional. It is not by itself an existence theorem. 11.4; 12.5
Weight Phase exponent or generator eigenvalue under a stated one-parameter transformation. 9.1
Wedge product Antisymmetric product of oriented form components; repeated directions give zero. 8.1; 8.3
Zero mode A profile in the kernel of a specified operator. A zero normal eigenvalue does not establish zero complete particle mass. 9.4
Compact profile and finite basin An exact supported shape and a nonlinear energy bound within a fixed-ball relative-profile class; not a dynamical invariance theorem. 12.6
Source-affine clock A rest Hamiltonian with derivative Omega with respect to each independent phase action. It preserves the common fundamental in the stated canonical chart. 12.7
Connectivity Laplacian A finite matrix of spatial coupling weights; rank C−K counts independent connections for K components. It is not another physical space. 12.7
Prescribed-probe susceptibility A controlled first shape response to an imposed gradient, before deriving a reciprocal particle-pair law. 12.8

C.3 Questions and evidence locators

If the question is… Start here
What does the exact count prove, and what remains physical? 3.1–3.3
Which numbers were prescribed or calibrated? 4.1–4.3, including both separate neutrino benchmarks
How strong is the alternative-depth test? 5.1 for the fixed-index diagnostic; 5.2 for the conditional unrestricted-index theorem
Why does the spatial pattern have half-spin? 6.1–6.3; distinguish its seed premise, full rotation law and continuous norm
Which component-carrier assumptions select depths? 7.1–7.3; 8.4
Does “three channels” already derive SU(3) color? 8.1–8.3; the answer requires the separate transformation and source assumptions
What does the relative-charge table establish? 9.1, then 10.1–10.2 for kinetic and interaction tests
Are the selected normal six directions the electron's six bound directions? 9.3
What is actually established at depth five? 9.4, including the distinct generator, texture and bubble assumptions
Is the magnetic moment a particle prediction? 11.3; the source coupling, preparation and normalization remain conditional
What did the localization numerics solve? 12.1–12.2, with the exact action, ten-space measure and grid table
What fails outside the quiet ansatz, and what repairs it? 12.3; the repair is scoped to the stated singlet escape and fixed-shape bounds
Are response tails mediator particles? 12.4; they solve an equation for an already retained field component
When is complete positive inertia established conditionally? 12.5, including stationary rest stress and boundary assumptions
Do all results belong to one established particle theory? 13.1–13.4, especially the carrier/action distinctions
Where are the exact sources, programs and reproduction rules? Appendix A; Appendix B
